# Code review

## Scope

This review covers the whole repository at `main` `932b9c8` (`docs(site): integrate unreleased fetch and status guides`). That revision is the first one on `main` that carries both the released `github contribution` slice (`v0.1.0`) and the `fetch`/`status`/workspace subsystem, which came over from `fetcher`. Every `file:line` below refers to `932b9c8`.

The review areas were:

- the `fetch` reconciliation stack: `internal/service/fetch`, `internal/state`, `internal/service/git`, `internal/command/fetch`, `internal/config/fetch*`;
- `status` and workspace discovery: `internal/service/status`, `internal/service/workspace`, `internal/command/status`;
- the contribution slice and the GitHub services: `internal/model/github/contribution`, `internal/command/github`, `internal/service/github`, `internal/pkg/time`;
- the rest of the code, meaning wiring, config, `makefile`, `go vanity` and `internal/pkg`;
- build and release engineering: `Makefile`, `bin/`, `.goreleaser.yml`, `.github/workflows`, `.github/scripts`, `.github/hooks`.

Only new defects are reported here. Anything already recorded is left out:

- the two earlier code reviews, [20260709T132530Z](20260709T132530Z.md) (C1–C12) and [20260710T095546Z](20260710T095546Z.md) (G1–G6);
- the defects and residues of the issue review [20260925T042955Z](20260925T042955Z.md) (I1–I7);
- the open issues in `.github/issues/`;
- the infrastructure port reports in `.github/reports/`, which already record `--fast-only` lint, Codecov OIDC on forks, docs notifications on PRs and the unscanned `notify` action pin.

A problem that shares a function with a known one is reported only when the failure differs, and the difference is named. [Status of earlier findings](#status-of-earlier-findings) re-derives the state of every earlier item on `932b9c8`.

Severity: **Crit** / **High** / **Med** / **Low**. Class: `correctness` · `security` · `api` · `build` · `docs` · `test` · `perf`.

## Validation and sources

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...` and `go mod verify` pass on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.1: 21 packages with tests, all `ok`.
- `govulncheck` was run as the latest release via `go run`, then again from `tools/`. It reports two reachable vulnerabilities (finding 2) and one unreachable one, GO-2026-5932, which is already known from the port reports.
- GitHub Actions, read-only through `gh run list/view`: *Continuous integration* fails on every `main` push from `47affe6` to `ad659f2`, in the Testing and Checking vulnerabilities jobs. The Linux test failure was reproduced in a `golang:1.27` container (git 2.47.3) as an unprivileged user, and its cause was confirmed by the same test passing once `git merge` gets an identity (finding 1).
- Almost every finding was reproduced. Each finding says whether it was reproduced or judged by reading. Reproductions used:
  - scratch `_test.go` files compiled into the packages through `go test -overlay`, which writes nothing into the tree;
  - a binary built from `932b9c8`, run against scratch Git repositories and state files with isolated `XDG_STATE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`;
  - `httptest` or fake transports in place of GitHub;
  - a scratch copy of the tracked files for `make` targets.
  About 60 scratch tests and scenarios were run in all.
- Also run: `goreleaser check` and a snapshot build with `dist` outside the tree; `bin/install` against the published `v0.1.0` (asset names and checksums match); `node --test .github/scripts/` (8/8 pass); `actionlint` (clean); `shellcheck` (info and style only); golangci-lint v2.14.0 with and without `--fast-only`.
- GitHub reads: issue states through `gh issue view`, and the release and tap metadata through `gh release view` and unauthenticated `curl`. Nothing was written to GitHub.
- Four subagents worked on the areas in parallel. This file merges their reports and removes overlaps: the owner-case defect was found twice and is reported once, as finding 8. The fetch reproductions and findings 1, 2, 4 and 14 were re-run by hand, and the cited lines were re-read.
- Not checked:
  - live GitHub behaviour: rate limits, secondary limits, `contributionsCollection` before 2008, and calendar week padding across years;
  - `fetch --apply` against a real workspace;
  - the `integration`-tagged tests;
  - Windows;
  - the TUI through a real terminal, beyond model-level tests and a geometry sweep of widths 1–140 and heights 1–30;
  - `doctor.yml` permissions, since no runs are retained.
- During the pass, one plan-only `fetch` and one `status` probe read the local user config and state file by mistake. Both were read-only and wrote nothing.

## 1. CI on main is red because a status test merges without a Git identity

`internal/service/status/git_test.go:218`

```go
cmd := exec.Command("git", "-C", path, "-c", "core.hooksPath=/dev/null", "merge", "conflict")
require.Error(t, cmd.Run())
```

Every other Git call in this file goes through `runGit` (`git_test.go:15-23`). That helper passes `user.name`, `user.email`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`. The one call that must fail, `git merge conflict`, is built by hand without them. On macOS, Git derives an identity from the account's GECOS name, so the merge stops at the conflict as intended. On a Linux runner the account has no GECOS name, so `git merge` stops earlier with `Committer identity unknown`. `require.Error` passes anyway. No conflict exists, and the next assertions fail: `Conflicts` and `Changed` are `0`, not `1` (`git_test.go:222-223`).

**Reproduction.** Run 36225532293 fails in both Testing jobs at `git_test.go:222` and `:223`, with `expected: 1, actual: 0`. In `golang:1.27` (git 2.47.3), `go test -run TestInspectRenameAndConflict ./internal/service/status/` fails the same way when run as a plain user. A bare `git merge` there prints `Committer identity unknown`. Adding `-c user.name=Test -c user.email=test@example.org` to that one command makes the test pass. On macOS the test passes as is.

**Consequence.** `main` has been red since the status work landed. That hides every other regression in CI. The test also checks the wrong thing: any merge failure satisfies `require.Error`.

**Fix.** Run the merge through the same options and environment as `runGit`. Assert on the merge output (`CONFLICT`) instead of on any error.

## 2. Reachable x/crypto SSH vulnerabilities fail the dependency gate and block the next release

`go.mod:81`

`golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0` (indirect, via go-git) has GO-2026-6354 and GO-2026-6355, both fixed in v0.56.0. Both let a server hang the client on a deadlocked SSH channel. `govulncheck` traces both to `internal/service/git/sync.go:111`: `Sync.Fetch` → `Repository.FetchContext` → `ssh.NewClientConn`.

**Reproduction.** `govulncheck ./...` prints `Your code is affected by 2 vulnerabilities from 1 module` and exits 3. The *Checking vulnerabilities* job of run 36225532293 fails with the same output.

**Consequence.** Three gates fail:

- `deps-check` (`Makefile:127`), which is part of `release-verify` (`Makefile:420`, `.github/workflows/cd.yml:71`), so the next tag cannot be released;
- the `vulns` job in `ci.yml`;
- the pre-push `verify` hook.

A `fetch` over SSH to a hostile or broken server can hang until the command timeout.

**Fix.** `go get golang.org/x/crypto@v0.56.0 && go mod tidy`. Dependabot watches `gomod` daily (`.github/dependabot.yml:7-12`), so also check why it has not opened this bump.

## 3. generate and go-generate disagree on the committed mocks so one of the gates always fails

`Makefile:372`, `Makefile:387`, `Makefile:420`, `internal/command/github/mocks_test.go:11`, `internal/service/git/mocks_test.go:12`

`ac08a33` committed the mocks exactly as mockgen writes them, so that `release-verify` (`… go-generate git-check`) keeps the tree clean. `generate` is `go-generate format` (`Makefile:372`). Its `goimports -local` step adds a blank line before the local import group. `verify` (`Makefile:387`) runs `generate … git-check`. Whichever form is committed, one of the two targets finds a dirty tree.

**Reproduction.** In a scratch copy of the tracked files, `make go-generate git-check` exits 0. `make generate git-check` fails with `make: *** [git-check] Error 1`, and `git diff` adds one blank line to each mock. The `v0.1.0` CI run 36156387977 failed at `Makefile:61: git-check`.

**Consequence.** Three gates fail on a clean tree even after finding 2 is fixed: the `ci.yml` `vulns` job (`ci.yml:98`), the `tools.yml` "Check git state" step (`tools.yml:57`) and the pre-push hook (`make deps-tidy verify`).

**Fix.** Pick one form. Either `go-generate` also runs `goimports -local` on generated files, or `release-verify` uses `generate`. Then regenerate the mocks once.

## 4. The default one-second test timeout fails make test and the pre-push hook

`Makefile:83`, `Makefile:187`

`TIMEOUT ?= 1s` is passed as `-timeout` to `go test -race`. The status tests start real Git processes and need several seconds under the race detector. CI passes only because it overrides `TIMEOUT=2m`.

**Reproduction.** `make test` fails with `panic: test timed out after 1s … TestInspectPushLock` and `FAIL internal/service/status`. `go test -race -timeout 2m ./internal/service/status/` passes in 6.3 s.

**Consequence.** The default `make`, `make check` and the pre-push hook fail locally on every run. So the hook gets bypassed, and a contributor cannot tell a real failure from the timeout.

**Fix.** Default `TIMEOUT` to the CI value of `2m`.

## 5. A prerelease tag is published as the latest release and pushed to the Homebrew tap

`.goreleaser.yml:93-98`, `.goreleaser.yml:14`, `.goreleaser.yml:43`, `.github/settings.json:3`

The release section sets no `prerelease`, and neither `brews` nor `homebrew_casks` sets `skip_upload`. GoReleaser v2.18.2 marks a release as prerelease only with `prerelease: auto|true` (`internal/pipe/release/release.go:75-82` in its source). It skips the tap only with `skip_upload: auto` (`internal/pipe/cask/cask.go:158`). The tag pattern in `.github/settings.json` accepts `-rc…` suffixes, and `release.mjs check` lets them through.

**Reproduction.** Judged by reading the config and the GoReleaser source. The history agrees: `gh release view v0.1.0-rc11` reports `"isPrerelease": false`.

**Consequence.** A tag such as `v0.2.0-rc1` becomes the "Latest" release and updates both the Formula and the Cask. Two install paths then deliver the release candidate: `bin/install`, which resolves `releases/latest`, and `brew upgrade`.

**Fix.** Add `release.prerelease: auto` and `skip_upload: auto` to both Homebrew sections.

## 6. Confirmation with a fallback token persists a false gone status

`internal/service/fetch/service.go:402-406`, `internal/service/fetch/service.go:513-527`

```go
profile := github.Profile{Name: rec.SourceProfile, Token: tokenFor(s.profiles, rec.SourceProfile)}
if profile.Token == "" {
    profile = github.Profile{Name: primaryProfile(s.profiles).Name, Token: primaryProfile(s.profiles).Token}
}
snap, err := s.deps.Confirmer.ConfirmByID(ctx, profile, rec.ID)
```

A tracked record that discovery did not return is re-confirmed by ID. If its `SourceProfile` was not selected, the primary profile's token is used instead. This happens with `--profile work`, with a renamed profile, or with `--config=""`, which yields a single `default` profile. GitHub answers 404 when a token cannot see a private repository, and `classifyConfirm` maps 404 to `ConfirmGone`. On `--apply` the result is saved as `remote_status = "gone"`. C9 was about the enum's zero value. Here a real 404 is misread.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_ProfileFallbackPersistsFalseGone`. The plan prints `orphan acme/priv → repository not found by GitHub ID (404)`, and the saved state holds `remote_status="gone"`.

**Consequence.** A narrowed run marks every private repository of the other profiles as deleted on GitHub. Offline `status` then shows those checkouts as gone until the next full run.

**Fix.** Treat a 404 as gone only when it comes from the record's own profile token. Otherwise skip the check, or classify the result as inaccessible or unverified.

## 7. Pins rendered from a state record produce a phantom conflict on every run after the first

`internal/service/fetch/service.go:136-146`, `internal/service/fetch/planner.go:135-139`, `internal/service/fetch/pinned.go:15-16`

To keep pinned paths inspectable, `Run` renders every record's pin a second time. It uses `github.RepoSnapshot{ID: rec.ID, Owner: rec.OwnerLogin, Name: rec.Name}` for that, a snapshot without visibility, default branch or flags. A per-repo `path = "pins/{{.Visibility}}/{{.Repo}}"` then renders as `pins/special` as well as the correct `pins/public/special`. The phantom path does not exist, so it becomes a conflict with ID 0. `docs/content/fetch.md` says per-repo pins keep the full rendering context. For a gone repository, which has no snapshot, the planner also puts the orphan row at the wrongly rendered path.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_PinTemplateRenderedFromRecord`. Run 1 adopts the repository and returns no error. Run 2 fetches it and adds `{"kind":"conflict","id":0,"path":".../special","reason":"pinned path is missing..."}`. It returns `apply incomplete: 0 action(s) failed, 1 conflict(s) unresolved`, which is exit 3.

**Consequence.** Every apply after the first exits 3 because of a conflict that cannot be resolved.

**Fix.** Use `rec.PinnedPath` when the record has one. Otherwise fill the snapshot from the record's `Visibility`, `DefaultBranch` and flags before rendering.

## 8. Owner logins are compared case-sensitively so discovery silently finds nothing

`internal/service/github/discovery_rest.go:101-104`, `internal/service/github/discovery_rest.go:122-130`, `internal/service/github/discovery_rest.go:144`, `internal/command/fetch/profiles.go:50-53`

```go
case owner == login:   // "OctoCat" != "octocat"
case members[owner]:   // "Octomation" not in {"octomation"}
if allow[s.Owner] {    // s.Owner is GitHub's canonical spelling
```

GitHub logins are case-insensitive, but these three comparisons are exact. Take `include_owners = ["OctoCat", "Octomation"]`:

- the token owner goes to `/users/OctoCat/repos?type=owner`, which returns public repositories only;
- the member organisation goes to `?type=public`;
- the allowlist then drops everything, because the canonical `s.Owner` never equals the configured spelling.

`--owner` goes through the same path.

**Reproduction.** Scratch tests with a fake transport that is case-insensitive like GitHub:

- lower-case owners give `endpoints=[/user/repos(2) /orgs/octomation/repos?type=all(2)]` and four snapshots;
- mixed-case owners give `endpoints=[/users/OctoCat/repos?type=owner(1) /orgs/Octomation/repos?type=public(2)] snapshots=[]`, with `err=nil`.

**Consequence.** `fetch` reports a successful discovery of zero repositories. Nothing new is cloned, private repositories are never requested, and every tracked record costs one `ConfirmByID` call.

**Fix.** Compare owners with `strings.EqualFold`, or lower-case the keys of `allow`, `members` and `login`. Apply the same to owner overrides and `Ignored`/`RepoOverride` matching.

## 9. A renamed repository whose old name is reused is re-cloned and its checkout adopted as the new one

`internal/service/fetch/adopter.go:122-125`, `internal/service/fetch/planner.go:288-299`, `internal/service/fetch/planner.go:324-351`

The adopter labels a checkout with the ID of whichever current repository has the checkout's `owner/name`. It never checks the state record that already claims that path under another ID. Take this state: ID 1 at `acme/old`. On GitHub, ID 1 has been renamed to `acme/new`, and a new ID 2 is `acme/old`. The checkout gets ID 2. ID 1 is then cloned from scratch, and ID 2 adopts the user's checkout.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_NameReuseMisadopts`. The plan is `adopt id=2 path=.../acme/old` and `clone id=1 path=.../acme/new`, with no move and no conflict.

**Consequence.** The design promises that a rename is a move, not a re-clone, and this breaks it. The checkout that holds the user's local branches is recorded as a different repository. The next `fetch --prune` pulls unrelated history into it and deletes its `refs/remotes/origin/*`, while a second clone appears next to it.

**Fix.** When a state record's path equals the checkout path and its ID differs from the name-derived ID, report a conflict. Alternatively, prefer the recorded ID when the stored `remote_url` matches the checkout's origin.

## 10. Overlapping owner and default templates clone one repository inside another

`internal/service/fetch/planner.go:472-495`, `internal/config/fetch.go:213-229`, `internal/service/workspace/scope.go:143-149`

The target-collision check compares exact path strings, and `Validate` does not reject owner templates that overlap the default template. Take `[[owners]] acme path = "{{.Repo}}"` together with the default `{{.Owner}}/{{.Repo}}`. Then `acme/bob` renders to `<root>/bob` and `bob/x` to `<root>/bob/x`. The workspace walk stops at the first `.git` (`SkipDir`), so `bob/x` is never seen again.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_NestedTargetsApply`. Run 1 clones `<root>/bob` and `<root>/bob/x` and reports `applied`. Run 2 reports `conflict bob/x → target path already exists and is not the expected repository` and returns `apply incomplete: … 1 conflict(s)`.

**Consequence.** One repository is cloned into another's working tree, where it shows up as untracked files. The plan never settles, and every later run exits 3.

**Fix.** Treat a target that is an ancestor or descendant of another target, or of a tracked path, as a conflict. Reject owner and default templates that can overlap in `Validate`.

## 11. A 403 or 451 while resolving one on-disk clone aborts the whole fetch

`internal/service/fetch/service.go:562-569`, `internal/service/fetch/adopter.go:126-130`

`profileNameResolver.ResolveByName` maps only 404 to "unknown". Every other status becomes a scan error, and `Run` returns before planning. Such statuses include a SAML SSO 403, a secondary rate-limit 403 and a 451.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_ResolverForbiddenAbortsRun`. The run fails with `scan workspace …: resolve sso-org/tool: … 403 Forbidden`. `acme/svc` is not cloned, and stdout is empty.

**Consequence.** One unrelated checkout in the managed layout blocks every fetch and clone. For example, a checkout of an organisation that requires SSO the token has not been authorised for.

**Fix.** For 401, 403 and 451, return ID 0 together with a per-clone error, so that the checkout becomes a conflict row like any other unverifiable checkout.

## 12. RateGuard mishandles 429 primary and 403 secondary rate limits

`internal/service/github/rate.go:94-101`, `internal/service/github/rate.go:151-158`

```go
case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden && remaining(resp) == 0:
    return g.untilReset(resp), true
case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests:
    return retryAfter(resp, g.backoff(attempt)), true
```

GitHub's REST documentation, "Exceeding the rate limit", was checked through Context7. A primary limit is a 403 **or** a 429 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, and clients must wait for `x-ratelimit-reset`. A secondary limit is a 403 **or** a 429 with `Retry-After`, or with no header, in which case clients wait at least a minute. The guard covers only a 403 with remaining 0. A 403 with `Retry-After` is not retried at all. A 429 with remaining 0 ignores the reset and retries on a short backoff. `retryAfter` also has no cap, while `untilReset` is capped at an hour. C10 covered transport-error retries, body replay and jitter; these status paths are separate.

**Reproduction.** Scratch probe:

- a secondary-limit 403 gives `status=403 attempts=1 waits=[]`;
- a primary-limit 429 with the reset 30 minutes away gives `attempts=6 total wait=12.7s waits=[410ms 814ms 1.2s 3.0s 7.2s]`, followed by the final 429.

**Consequence.** Discovery fails on the first secondary limit. During a primary lockout it sends six requests in 13 seconds, the behaviour GitHub warns can get an integration banned, and then fails anyway.

**Fix.** For a 403 or a 429: wait until the reset when remaining is 0; otherwise honour `Retry-After` up to a cap; otherwise wait at least 60 seconds with backoff.

## 13. Report-only orphan rows count as duplicates and turn the managed checkout into an error

`internal/service/status/service.go:161-188`, `internal/service/status/service.go:73-81`

```go
for _, row := range rows { duplicates[strings.ToLower(row.Repository)]++ }
...
if duplicates[key] > 1 && pins[key] == "" { row.Status, row.Error = "error", "multiple checkouts ..." }
```

The duplicate counter includes rows that are already marked `out-of-scope` or `duplicate-pin`. The error then overwrites `Status` on every such row. A stale `previous_paths` copy has the same effect when the active pin is a workspace pin: it is labelled `duplicate-pin`, but `pins[key]` is never set.

**Reproduction.** Scenario: state record 7 `acme/tool` at `A/public/acme/tool`, and a second clone with the same origin at `B/public/acme/tool`.

- `status --root B --format=json` returns two rows with `"status": "error"` and `"multiple checkouts for this repository; select one with a per-repo path"`. The first row also carries `"orphan_reason": "out-of-scope"`. The command then prints `Error: could not inspect 2 checkout(s)` and exits 1.
- `status --config fetch.toml` alone exits 0 with one row.

**Consequence.** The managed checkout loses its Git status, and the command exits 1. The docs say orphan labels are report-only and do not replace Git status, and `fetch` treats the same layout correctly: the planner skips out-of-scope records before looking for duplicates.

**Fix.** Leave rows that have an `OrphanReason` out of `duplicates`, and never overwrite an orphan row's status.

## 14. Checkouts without a GitHub origin are keyed by directory name and reported as duplicates

`internal/service/status/service.go:47`, `internal/service/status/git.go:89-93`, `internal/service/status/service.go:162-188`

`name := filepath.Base(path)` becomes the identity whenever `origin` is missing, the remote has another name, or the URL is local or `file://`, because `remoteName` then returns `""`. The duplicate check keys on that basename.

**Reproduction.** `git init public/alice/tool` and `git init public/bob/tool` under one root, then `status --format=plain`. Both rows read `tool │ main │ ? │ error: multiple checkouts for this repository; select one with a per-repo path`, followed by `Error: could not inspect 2 checkout(s)` and exit 1.

**Consequence.** Two unrelated repositories, typically new projects not pushed yet, lose their Git status, and the command fails. `fetch` skips such checkouts, so the two commands disagree.

**Fix.** Check for duplicates only among rows whose `owner/name` identity comes from origin or state, never among basename fallbacks.

## 15. One unreadable directory under a pin aborts status and fetch

`internal/service/workspace/scope.go:89-94`, `internal/service/workspace/scope.go:123-132`, `internal/service/workspace/scope.go:143-152`

Under a pin, `descend` has no depth bound: `Within(pin, path)` walks every directory that is not a checkout. Any `walkErr`, and any `Lstat(.git)` error other than "not exist", is returned as fatal. The existing test covers only unreadable directories outside the layout.

**Reproduction.** `pins = ["prototyping"]`, with `prototyping/app/pgdata` set to mode 000. `status --config fetch.toml` prints `Error: scan …: lstat …/prototyping/app/pgdata/.git: permission denied`, exits 1 and prints no rows.

**Consequence.** A root-owned Docker volume or a `0700` database directory inside a non-Git project under a pin breaks both `status` and `fetch`, which share `Scope.Walk`. Non-repository trees under a pin, such as `node_modules`, are also walked in full.

**Fix.** Under pins, skip unreadable directories that are not checkout candidates, or turn them into warning rows. Bound the descent, or prune well-known vendor directories.

## 16. A templated repos rule without a state record pins a wrongly rendered path

`internal/service/status/service.go:99-117`

When no state record exists, `rec` holds only `{ID}` or `{Owner, Name}`. `PinnedPath` renders `{{.Owner}}`, `{{.Repo}}` and `{{.Visibility}}` as empty strings, and `filepath.Clean` collapses the empty components. The result is then added as an explicit pin. This is the offline counterpart of finding 7; the missing context is the state record, not snapshot fields.

**Reproduction.** Rule `[[repos]] match = { id = 42 }`, `path = "<scratch>/ext/{{.Owner}}/{{.Repo}}"`, with an empty state. `status --config fetch.toml` shows a single row, `ext │ — │ ? │ error: stat …/ext/.git: no such file or directory`, and exits 1.

**Consequence.** Until `fetch` has run, status shows a phantom error row and exits 1. When the collapsed path is itself a repository, status inspects that repository instead and marks it pinned. Examples are `~/{{.Repo}}` collapsing to the home directory, or a monorepo parent. Other checkouts of it are then labelled `duplicate-pin`.

**Fix.** Offline, use a rule's path as a pin only when it is literal or every field it references is known. Otherwise show an "unresolved pin" row and inspect nothing.

## 17. Unknown subcommands print help and exit 0 and the test for it cannot fail

`internal/command/root.go:20`, `internal/command/github/root.go:14`, `internal/command/golang/root.go:7`, `internal/command/makefile/root.go:7`, `main_test.go:21-25`

The group commands set `Args: cobra.NoArgs` but define no `Run`. For a command that cannot run, cobra returns `flag.ErrHelp` before it validates arguments, and then treats that as success. `main_test.go` replaces `exit` with an assertion that is never called on this path. The "failure" subtest therefore checks nothing.

**Reproduction.** Built binary:

- `maintainer fecth`, `github bogus`, `go bogus`, `makefile bogus` and `github contribution bogus` each print help and exit 0;
- an overlay test that calls `main()` with `root unknown` records `exit called=false`.

**Consequence.** A mistyped subcommand in a script or a cron job succeeds silently, and the test gives false confidence.

**Fix.** Give the group commands a `RunE` that returns an unknown-command error when arguments are present. Make the test assert that `exit` was called with 1.

## 18. Invalid flag values exit 1 although the docs promise 2

`main.go:59-65`, `internal/command/root.go`, `internal/command/fetch/root.go:104-107`, `docs/content/fetch.md:289`, `docs/content/fetch.md:299`

The exit-code tables in the docs map invalid options to 2. No `SetFlagErrorFunc` is set, so pflag parse errors reach `main` as plain errors, which exit 1. Validation is also inconsistent: `status --concurrency=0` exits 2, but `fetch --concurrency=-1` is silently replaced by the config value, although the docs require a positive value or 0.

**Reproduction.** `status --concurrency=abc`, `status --bogus` and `fetch --timeout=soon` exit 1. `status --concurrency=0` exits 2.

**Consequence.** Automation cannot tell a usage error from a transport or Git failure.

**Fix.** `root.SetFlagErrorFunc(func(_ *cobra.Command, err error) error { return exit.WithUser(err) })`. Wrap `Args` validation the same way, and reject a negative `--concurrency` in `fetch`.

## 19. A rename that changes only letter case is a permanent conflict on macOS

`internal/service/fetch/occupancy.go:29-30`, `internal/service/fetch/planner.go:373-378`, `internal/service/git/sync.go:132`

When `octocat` is renamed to `OctoCat`, the new target differs from `rec.Path` only in case. On APFS, which is case-insensitive by default, `os.Lstat(target)` finds the repository's own checkout, and occupancy marks the target foreign. The fetcher specification names this risk but plans nothing for it.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_CaseOnlyRename`, on a filesystem confirmed case-insensitive. Both the plan and the apply give `conflict id=1 … "target path already exists and is not the expected repository"`.

**Consequence.** The repository is never fetched again, and its remote is never updated. The message is also wrong, because the "foreign" target is the repository itself.

**Fix.** When `strings.EqualFold(target, rec.Path)` holds and `os.SameFile` confirms it, rename in two steps through a temporary name, or only update the remote.

## 20. Filters do not gate adoption although the docs say they do

`internal/service/fetch/planner.go:288-299`, `docs/content/fetch.md:81`, `internal/config/fetch.go:79`

The docs and the config comment say filters gate "new clone/adopt decisions". The `filtered` flag is checked only on the clone branch.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_FilterDoesNotGateAdopt`. With `ExcludeForks` and `ExcludeArchived` set, an archived fork gives `kind=adopt … filtered=false`.

**Consequence.** With `exclude_forks = true`, existing fork checkouts are still adopted and then fetched on every run.

**Fix.** Skip filtered snapshots on the adopt branch, or reword the docs and the comment to say that filters gate clones only.

## 21. The owner flag does not limit work to that owner

`internal/command/fetch/root.go:56`, `docs/content/fetch.md:122-127`, `internal/service/fetch/service.go:176-208`

The flag help says "limit work to these owners", and `fetch.md:122-123` says `--owner acme` "processes only `acme`". Yet tracked checkouts of other owners are confirmed again, added back to the plan and fetched. `fetch.md:125-127` describes this actual behaviour, so the page contradicts itself.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_OwnerFlagStillFetchesOtherOwners`: `api_calls=3 fetched=[…/acme/svc …/other/tool]`, summary `fetch=2`.

**Consequence.** A narrowed run still touches the network for the whole workspace, and spends an API call on every out-of-scope checkout.

**Fix.** Either leave out-of-scope checkouts alone when `--owner` or `--profile` is set, or correct the help text and `fetch.md:122-123`.

## 22. One repository whose path cannot be rendered aborts the whole plan

`internal/service/fetch/planner.go:278-281`, `internal/service/fetch/occupancy.go:25-28`, `internal/service/fetch/service.go:209-211`, `internal/service/fetch/service.go:233-235`

A layout such as `{{.Owner}}/{{.Repo}}@{{.DefaultBranch}}` passes `Validate`. A default branch `release/v1` then renders an extra path component, `Resolve` fails, and the error ends the run instead of producing a conflict for that one repository.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_SingleBadRenderAbortsPlan`. The planner returns `actions=0`, with `resolve path for acme/odd (id=2): rendered path "/work/acme/odd@release/v1" is outside workspace layout`.

**Consequence.** A single repository with an unusual branch name blocks the fetch for every other repository.

**Fix.** Turn per-snapshot `Resolve` errors into `KindConflict` actions that carry the reason.

## 23. UpdateRemote is a silent no-op under insteadOf and corrupts origin with a push URL

`internal/service/git/sync.go:152-172`

When a `url.<base>.insteadOf` rule in the repository's own `.git/config` applies, go-git's `RemoteConfig.marshal` writes back its saved original URLs, including `pushurl` values. That overrides both `remote.URLs` and the raw `SetOption`, and `UpdateRemote` still returns nil.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_UpdateRemoteWithInsteadOf`:

- without a push URL, `UpdateRemote` returns `err=<nil>` and `origins after=[https://github.com/acme/old.git]`, unchanged;
- with `pushurl = no_push`, it returns `origins=[https://github.com/acme/old.git no_push]`.

**Consequence.** The applier records the new `RemoteURL` in state while the disk keeps the old one, so `update_remote` is planned again on every run. With a push lock, which is the dotfiles `git_lock` convention the status Lock column reads, `origin` gains `no_push` as a fetch URL. The next inspection then reports an ambiguous remote.

**Fix.** Edit only the raw config subsection and do not marshal the typed remote. Re-inspect after writing, and fail if the fetch URL did not change.

## 24. Human output shortens paths by string prefix instead of by path component

`internal/service/fetch/reporter.go:244-249`

**Reproduction.** Scratch test `TestScratch_ReporterShortPrefix`. With root `/work`, the path `/workspace/acme/x` renders as `at <root>space/acme/x`.

**Consequence.** Pin and conflict paths outside the root are shown wrongly. A sibling pin such as `~/Development-old` next to the root `~/Development` is a realistic case.

**Fix.** Shorten only when `workspace.Within(root, path)` holds, using `filepath.Rel`.

## 25. A Git repository at an unmanaged level hides every checkout below it

`internal/service/workspace/scope.go:143-149`

```go
if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
    if s.Contains(path) { ... }
    return filepath.SkipDir
```

The walk checks for `.git` before it checks `Contains`. It then skips the directory even when the directory is outside the layout, and emits no row and no warning.

**Reproduction.** Status reports:

- with only `public/o/r` a repository: one checkout;
- after `git init public/o`: `0 checkouts`, exit 0;
- after `git init` of the root itself: again `0 checkouts`, exit 0.

**Consequence.** Checkouts known only from disk vanish from status with exit 0. The status docs say failures produce error rows, not clean results. `fetch` loses them too and may plan a clone into an existing directory. Occupancy then catches that as a conflict, but the report is misleading.

**Fix.** Stop descent only at paths within scope. At a prefix level, continue past a `.git` or report a warning row.

## 26. The implicit root fails when the working directory is reached through a symlink

`internal/command/status/root.go:45`, `internal/service/fetch/pathtemplate.go:41`, `internal/service/workspace/scope.go:133-136`

The default root `.` comes from `os.Getwd`, which returns the logical `$PWD`. `WalkDir` then runs `Lstat` on it and rejects a symlink.

**Reproduction.** With `ln -s real link`, `status --format=plain` works in `real`. In `link` it prints `Error: … workspace path …/link is not a directory (symlink roots are not followed)` and exits 1.

**Consequence.** A bare `maintainer status` fails in a symlinked workspace, and the error blames configuration the user never wrote. The docs warn only about configured symlinks.

**Fix.** For the implicit root, resolve the working directory with `filepath.EvalSymlinks`, or name the symlinked cwd in the error.

## 27. Status error rows drop Git's stderr and blame the wrong step

`internal/service/status/git.go:59-61`, `internal/service/status/git.go:84-87`

`cmd.Output()` collects stderr in `ExitError.Stderr`, but only `err` is formatted. The lock probe runs first, so every broken repository is reported as a failure of `git config`.

**Reproduction.** A `.git` gitfile with `gitdir: /nonexistent/x` gives `"error": "git config: exit status 128"`. `git status` in the same directory says `fatal: not a git repository`.

**Consequence.** Error rows cannot be diagnosed: dubious ownership, a broken gitfile and a corrupt HEAD all read the same.

**Fix.** Append the trimmed `ExitError.Stderr` to the message, and run the lock probe after `git status`.

## 28. Sorting while the filter hides the selected row moves the highlight

`internal/service/status/terminal.go:76-80`

```go
m.selection.Index = max(0, slices.Index(m.visible, m.anchor))
```

When the filter hides `anchor`, the screen highlights `visible[0]`, but `anchor` still points at the hidden row. Every later `rebuild` falls back to index 0.

**Reproduction.** Scratch model test with rows `alpha`, `beta1`, `beta2`, `gamma`:

1. `G` selects `gamma`;
2. filtering on `beta` highlights `beta1`;
3. `s` keeps `beta1`;
4. a second `s`, sorting descending, highlights `beta2`.

**Consequence.** The status docs say "sorting preserves the selected checkout", and this breaks that. The path in the footer changes under the user.

**Fix.** When the anchor is hidden, sort around the highlighted row. Keep the original anchor to restore once the filter is cleared.

## 29. Status runs repository-configured clean filters during an offline inspection

`internal/service/status/git.go:47`

`git` runs with `-c core.fsmonitor=false`, which shows that repository-configured programs are meant to stay out of an inspection. `git status` and `git diff HEAD` still run `filter.<name>.clean` and `filter.<name>.process` on files whose stat data has changed.

**Reproduction.** `.gitattributes` has `* filter=evil`, `.git/config` has `filter.evil.clean = "sh -c 'echo ran >> PWNED; cat'"`, and a tracked file is modified. `status --format=plain` shows `+1/-0 · 1f`, and `PWNED` contains `ran` four times.

**Consequence.** Any pinned or discovered directory with a hostile `.git/config` runs commands during a read-only `status`. This is Git's own trust model, but not the hardening the fsmonitor option implies.

**Fix.** Decide the threat model. Either document that status trusts repository config as `git status` does, or neutralise the configured filters (`-c filter.<name>.clean= -c filter.<name>.process=`).

## 30. lookup prints its only output to stderr and histogram bypasses the command writer

`internal/command/github/contribution/helper.go:293`, `internal/command/github/contribution/histogram.go:62`

`TableView` writes with `cmd.PrintErrln`. That split is intended for `suggest`, whose stdout carries only the timestamp, and `lookup` shares it although it has no other output. `histogram` writes with `fmt.Printf`, so `cmd.SetOut` has no effect on it. The known [[issue-136]] residue concerns `suggest` only.

**Reproduction.** End-to-end overlay test against a fake GitHub: `lookup 2026-01-01/2` produces `stdout=""`, with the whole table on stderr.

**Consequence.** `lookup > week.txt`, `lookup | less` and `lookup | grep Monday` all get nothing, although `docs/content/contributions.md` presents the table as the command's output.

**Fix.** Pass the writer into `TableView`: stdout for `lookup`, stderr for `suggest`. Use `cmd.Printf` in `histogram`.

## 31. suggest with an old anchor sends one GraphQL request per year up to now

`internal/command/github/contribution/suggest.go:152-154`, `internal/service/github/contribution.go:15-17`, `internal/service/github/contribution.go:65-75`

`SuggestScope` extends the range to now, and `ContributionHeatMap` requests every calendar year from the anchor to the current year, including years before GitHub existed. A comment says "the span is bounded by the commands", which holds for `lookup`, `histogram` and `snapshot` but not for `suggest`.

**Reproduction.** End-to-end test: `suggest --short --target=6 1970` makes 58 GraphQL calls. A repository whose HEAD dates from 2010 makes 17.

**Consequence.** The command is slow and more likely to hit secondary limits. The GraphQL client has no RateGuard. The answer almost always comes from the first weeks after the anchor.

**Fix.** Fetch year by year from the anchor and stop at the first year that yields a suggestion. Skip years before 2008 or before the account's `createdAt`.

## 32. RangeByMonths overshoots the month end for non-zero spans

`internal/pkg/time/range.go:80-93`

`max` is the last nanosecond of the month. `max.AddDate(0, n, 0)` normalises "31 February" to 3 March. `RangeByMonths` has no tests, and the CLI calls it only with 0, so the defect is latent.

**Reproduction.** Scratch test:

- `RangeByMonths(2026-01-15, 1, false)` gives `[2026-01-01, 2026-03-03T23:59:59.999999999Z]`;
- `(2026-08-01, 1, false)` gives an end of `2026-10-01T23:59:59.999999999Z`.

**Consequence.** Any month span, such as the one [[issue-45]] asks for, would include up to three extra days.

**Fix.** Compute the end from the shifted first day, `min.AddDate(0, n+1, 0).Add(-time.Nanosecond)`, and add tests.

## 33. The release preflight accepts a tap token that cannot write

`.github/scripts/release.mjs:365-369`

The preflight only reads `repos/octolab/homebrew-tap`. The tap is public, so any valid token passes, read-only or wrongly scoped ones included.

**Reproduction.** An unauthenticated `GET https://api.github.com/repos/octolab/homebrew-tap` returns 200 with `"private": false`. An invalid bearer token gets 401. A valid token without write access was not available to test.

**Consequence.** GoReleaser creates the release and uploads the assets, then fails pushing the Formula and the Cask. The result is a half-published release, which is what the preflight exists to prevent.

**Fix.** Check `permissions.push` in the repository response, or probe a harmless write such as creating an unreferenced blob.

## 34. makefile build reads a multi-file include or a trailing comment as one file name

`internal/command/makefile/pkg.go:72`, `internal/command/makefile/pkg.go:78`

This differs from I6, which is about include cycles and include resolution.

**Reproduction.** `make -f` accepts both of these, but `makefile build` does not:

- `include x.mk y.mk` fails with `open x.mk y.mk: no such file or directory`;
- `include x.mk # shared vars` fails with `open x.mk # shared vars: …`.

Both exit 1.

**Consequence.** Valid Makefiles do not assemble.

**Fix.** Strip `#` comments, split the rest with `strings.Fields`, and expand each name.

## 35. The vanity publisher never closes the pages it writes

`internal/model/golang/vanity/publisher.go:38`

`publisher.fs.Create` opens `index.html`. The file is never closed, so write-back errors from `Close` are lost too.

**Reproduction.** With `ulimit -n 64` and 100 packages, `go vanity build` fails with `open site/toolkit/p61/index.html: too many open files`, exits 1 and leaves 59 pages behind.

**Consequence.** Large module sets fail midway, and a failed flush goes unnoticed.

**Fix.** Close the file after `tpl.Execute` and return the `Close` error.

## 36. A vanity module without packages gets no page

`internal/model/golang/vanity/issue6.go:12-24`, `internal/model/golang/vanity/publisher.go:36`

`fill` walks only the listed packages. A module with an `import` but no `packages` produces nothing, not even its root page. I7, a non-terminating loop, concerns packages outside the prefix; this one concerns an empty list.

**Reproduction.** Overlay test: the module `go.octolab.org/nopkgs` produces no file, and the run exits 0.

**Consequence.** `go get` on that module path gets a 404 from the vanity host, and nothing reports the gap.

**Fix.** Always include the module prefix in `fill`.

## 37. bin/activate can close the calling shell and computes a wrong GOBIN

`bin/activate:3`, `bin/activate:86`, `bin/activate:99`

The file is meant to be sourced, but `release` calls `exit` when a repository has no tags. The script also sets `pipefail` in the caller's shell, and builds `GOBIN` by concatenating the working directory with `$0`'s directory.

**Reproduction.**

- In a repository without tags, `bash -c 'source bin/activate; release; echo survived'` prints "no have any release" and never reaches the `echo`.
- Sourcing by absolute path gives `GOBIN=<repo>/<repo>/bin/darwin/arm64`.

**Consequence.** An interactive terminal closes, and tools land in a non-existent directory.

**Fix.** Use `return 1`, resolve the directory with `cd "$(dirname …)" && pwd`, and do not set shell options in a sourced file.

### Consequences for the backlog

- The mirror is stale. [[issue-445]], [[issue-446]] and [[issue-457]] are closed on GitHub but `state: OPEN` in `.github/issues/`. A `dump` fixes it. This pass did not run one, to leave `.github/issues/` untouched.
- The confirmed defects behind [[issue-148]], [[issue-189]] and [[issue-284]] are fixed on `main` (`97bdfcb`), and those issues ask for nothing else. They are candidates for closing. [[issue-70]], [[issue-133]] and [[issue-155]] also had their defect fixed, but each asks for more (a refactor, a feature, an argument grammar). Re-assess them rather than close them.
- [[issue-30]] is open although `v0.1.0` is tagged and published. Whether it closes is the owner's decision under the release plan.
- Findings 1–4 should be fixed together, because only then does *Continuous integration* go green again. Until then, CI cannot report any regression, including one in the findings above.

### Post-pass reconciliation

After the pass, `dump` was run together with the ProjectsV2 boards, and `verify` was run against GitHub. The dump rewrote three mirror files: [[issue-445]], [[issue-446]] and [[issue-457]] are now `state: CLOSED` with `stateReason: COMPLETED`. The first item under [Consequences for the backlog](#consequences-for-the-backlog) is therefore resolved.

`verify` then reported:

- issues: 126 files for 126 on GitHub, with 0 differences in body, title, labels, milestone, state, stateReason and updatedAt;
- comments: 47 notes for 47 on GitHub, with no missing or dead URLs;
- milestones: 2 for 2, with 0 differences;
- boards: 2, unchanged by the dump.

No verdict above changed.
